# Tugrul Guner

Canonical profile: https://tugrul.modepot.io/

Tugrul Guner is an AI Engineering Manager at CDAI in Toronto, Canada. He directly manages four people, provides technical and cross-functional leadership across two pods of five and seven people, and oversees seven projects. His leadership model combines portfolio-level strategy and organizational responsibility with hands-on involvement in difficult engineering decisions.

He created ModePot, an open-source family of frameworks, tools, engines, and games built around simpler APIs, modern runtimes, performance, and explicit boundaries between deterministic software and agent-owned decisions.

## Story

Tugrul began coding and working with machine learning during his master's degree in 2012, learned traditional machine-learning approaches, participated in Kaggle competitions, and practiced feature engineering. He later used deep learning for computer vision with microscope images during his first postdoctoral appointment and for image reconstruction during his second. As the models became more capable, he became increasingly interested in the backends, deployment, infrastructure, and operating practices required to make AI reliable beyond an experiment. That path led him into MLOps and production AI.

ModePot is where he builds tools and systems he wants to exist. Passionately Curious makes difficult scientific ideas accessible to broad audiences. His personal essays examine ambition, mortality, curiosity, and the future behind his work.

## Career

- AI Engineering Manager, CDAI (2026–present): directly manages four people and provides technical and cross-functional leadership across two separate pods of five and seven. After leading one pod to a 2.5x increase in delivery velocity, he was given responsibility for the second pod. He oversees seven projects; helped the team launch three products; and contributed to a recommendation system that improved menu-item attachment rate 4x. Initiated the AI & Science channel, co-hosts the company-wide AI Center of Excellence meeting, and created recurring social events.
- Technical Manager and AI Architect, Haptiq (2025–2026): built the AI team and first AI infrastructure, created its high-performance engineering culture, led client and executive conversations, and helped sell the company's first AI product to businesses as part of more than $2 million in new revenue.
- Lead MLOps Engineer, Arteria AI (2024–2025)
- Senior MLOps Engineer, Arteria AI (2022–2024)

## Leadership ambition

As a manager, Tugrul is ambitious about creating high-performing teams where talented people take ownership and raise the standard for one another. He gives people the context and authority to make good decisions, with explicit ownership and standards that make autonomy work. As he takes on greater organizational scope, he wants to stay close enough to the technology to make sound decisions while helping people grow into harder problems and challenge ideas with evidence.

## Education and research

- MBA, Quantic School of Business and Technology (2025)
- Ph.D., Materials Science and Engineering, Izmir Institute of Technology (2018)
- Postdoctoral Fellow, University of Ottawa (2021–2022): applied deep learning to quantum-optics and beam-shaping research and contributed to a CFI project.
- Postdoctoral Fellow, Institut national de la recherche scientifique (INRS) (2018–2021): operated and maintained ultrafast transmission electron microscopy systems, developed measurement algorithms, and supported MSc and Ph.D. researchers.
- 30 journal publications and one patent
- Google Scholar: 1,023 citations, h-index 19, i10-index 21 as of September 2026
- Publications: https://scholar.google.com.tr/citations?user=RznlT4AAAAAJ&hl=en

## Writing

Tugrul created Passionately Curious because years in research showed him how much discovery stays buried in language written for specialists. The evidence-led newsletter brings questions from physics, AI, and biology to readers from any background by following the mechanism rather than summarizing papers and by keeping uncertainty visible. He has also published seven Medium essays about technology, scientific curiosity, ambition, mortality, and building the future. Two personal essays that describe his outlook are “Legacy Is Overrated. I Want to Be Alive for What Comes Next.” and “Nothing Is Waiting For Us. And That’s Why I Care.”
